rules.title: A game value can be a negative number.
rules.text: 2.10. A game value can be a negative number.

rules.title: When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
rules.text:
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit has 2 power. An effect reduces its power by 3. The Unit has -1 power, but is treated as having 0 power when attacking, fighting, or when a card effect references its power. If it then gains +2 power, that Unit has 1 power. The order of these effects being applied does not alter this outcome.

rules.title: A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number.
rules.text: 2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

rules.title: During the “React Step” of an attack, the defending player has an opportunity to react.
rules.text: 9.7. During the “React Step” of an attack, the defending player has an opportunity to react. They may take as many reactions as they want, in any order they choose.

rules.title: You may only take reactions during the React Step of an attack, and only if you are the defending player.
rules.text: 9.7.1. You may only take reactions during the React Step of an attack, and only if you are the defending player.

rules.text: 9.14. When the React Step ends, the attack continues. If the attack target is a Unit, proceed to the Fight Step. If the attack target is a Gig area, proceed to the Steal Step.

rules.title: The Fight Step only happens if the attack target is a Unit.
rules.text: 9.15. The Fight Step only happens if the attack target is a Unit. If the attack target is a Gig Area, the Steal Step happens instead.

rules.title: During the “Fight Step” of an attack, the attacking Unit and the defending Unit fight.
rules.text: 9.16. During the “Fight Step” of an attack, the attacking Unit and the defending Unit fight.

rules.text: 9.16.1. At the start of the Fight Step, apply effects that last “while fighting” and variations thereof.

rules.title: A “fight” is a game process in which two opposing Units compare power to determine at least one loser and potentially…
rules.text: 9.17. A “fight” is a game process in which two opposing Units compare power to determine at least one loser and potentially one winner.

rules.title: A Unit wins a fight when it has a higher power than the opposing Unit.
rules.text: 9.17.1. A Unit wins a fight when it has a higher power than the opposing Unit.

rules.title: When a Unit wins a fight, the opposing Unit always loses, regardless of power.
rules.text: 9.17.1.1. When a Unit wins a fight, the opposing Unit always loses, regardless of power.

rules.title: A Unit loses a fight when it has equal or lower power than the opposing Unit.
rules.text: 9.17.2. A Unit loses a fight when it has equal or lower power than the opposing Unit.

rules.text: 9.17.3. If both Units in a fight have the same power, neither Unit wins and both Units lose the fight.

rules.text: 9.17.4. If a card effect says that a Unit wins or loses a fight, it supersedes any win or loss status determined by power comparison.

rules.title: When you determine the loser(s), any effects triggered by the fight (i.e.
rules.text: 9.18. When you determine the loser(s), any effects triggered by the fight (i.e. “when this Unit fights,” “when this Unit loses a fight,” etc.) become pending. Both players must resolve all pending effects before they may defeat the loser(s).

rules.title: After resolving all effects triggered by the fight, resolve the fight’s result.
rules.text: 9.19. After resolving all effects triggered by the fight, resolve the fight’s result.

rules.title: When a Unit loses a fight, the opposing Unit defeats it as a result.
rules.text: 9.19.1. When a Unit loses a fight, the opposing Unit defeats it as a result.

rules.text: 9.19.2. A Unit with 0 power cannot defeat a Unit as the result of a fight.

rules.text: 9.19.3. If an effect prevents a Unit from being defeated in a fight, it is still a loser that has lost the fight, it only ignores the resulting defeat.

rules.text: 9.20. After resolving all effects triggered by the fight’s result, the Fight Step and the attack ends. See ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL > Ending an Attack.

rules.title: The Steal Step only happens if the attack target is a Gig area.
rules.text: 9.21. The Steal Step only happens if the attack target is a Gig area. If the attack target is a Unit, the Fight Step happens instead.

rules.title: If the attacked Gig area has no Gigs in it when the Steal Step begins, no Gigs can be or are stolen.
rules.text: 9.22. If the attacked Gig area has no Gigs in it when the Steal Step begins, no Gigs can be or are stolen.

rules.text: 9.23. During the “Steal Step” of an attack, the attacker attempts to steal one or more Gig dice from the defending Gig area.

rules.title: At the start of the Steal Step, before choosing which Gigs are stolen, apply effects that last “while stealing” and v…
rules.text: 9.23.1. At the start of the Steal Step, before choosing which Gigs are stolen, apply effects that last “while stealing” and variations thereof. Apply any other effects that modify, prevent, or restrict the attacker’s power or ability to steal.

rules.title: The number of Gigs an attacker steals is based on its power.
rules.text: 9.23.2. The number of Gigs an attacker steals is based on its power.

rules.title: If the attacking Unit has 0 power, it steals 0 Gigs.
rules.text: 9.23.2.1. If the attacking Unit has 0 power, it steals 0 Gigs.

rules.title: If the attacking Unit has 1 or more power, it steals X Gigs (rounded down) according to this formula, where P = the a…
rules.text:
9.23.2.2. If the attacking Unit has 1 or more power, it steals X Gigs (rounded down) according to this formula, where P = the attacking Unit’s power.

`X = (P / 10) + 1)`

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit with 1 to 9 power steals 1 Gig. A Unit with 10 to 19 power steals 2 Gigs. Continue this pattern for higher power values.

rules.title: The attacking player chooses which Gigs the attacker will steal from the attacked Gig area.
rules.text: 9.23.3. The attacking player chooses which Gigs the attacker will steal from the attacked Gig area.

rules.title: An attacking player may choose to steal any Gig in the defending Gig area, regardless of its value.
rules.text: 9.23.3.1. An attacking player may choose to steal any Gig in the defending Gig area, regardless of its value.

rules.text: 9.26.3. The attack target is no longer a legal attack target for the attacking Unit.

rules.text: 9.27.2. If an attack ends while an effect or pending effect is resolving, finish resolving that effect or pending effect.

rules.text: 9.28. When an attack ends, resolve any pending effects that are already pending for the current timing window.

rules.title: To “resolve” an effect, follow the instructions of that effect in the order they appear.
rules.text: 10.2. To “resolve” an effect, follow the instructions of that effect in the order they appear.

rules.title: Always resolve as much of an effect as possible.
rules.text: 10.2.1. Always resolve as much of an effect as possible. See GOLDEN RULES > Resolve as Much as Possible.

rules.title: Effects cannot interrupt the activation or resolution of other effects.

rules.title: After an effect resolves, perform any required rule processing before resolving a new one or taking any actions.
rules.text: 10.2.5. After an effect resolves, perform any required rule processing before resolving a new one or taking any actions.

rules.title: An effect may include conditions.
rules.text: 10.3. An effect may include conditions. A “condition” is a requirement that must be true for an effect to apply, become pending, and resolve. (Conditions are often “if” or “when” clauses.)

rules.title: If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect.
rules.text: 10.3.1. If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect.

rules.title: A condition is not a cost unless it is specifically within a cost.
rules.text: 10.3.2. A condition is not a cost unless it is specifically within a cost. See Cost.

rules.title: A condition within an effect’s resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves.
rules.text: 10.3.3. A condition within an effect’s resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves.

rules.title: If you have multiple pending effects, you may resolve them in any order.
rules.text: 10.12. If you have multiple pending effects, you may resolve them in any order.

rules.text: 10.13. If both players control pending effects at the same time, the turn player resolves all their pending effects before their Rival resolves all of theirs.

rules.title: A triggered effect has a trigger condition.
rules.text: 10.16. A triggered effect has a trigger condition.

rules.title: A triggered effect becomes pending when (and only if) its trigger condition is met.
rules.text: 10.16.1. A triggered effect becomes pending when (and only if) its trigger condition is met.

rules.title: If multiple triggered effects trigger at the same time, they all become pending.
rules.text: 10.16.2. If multiple triggered effects trigger at the same time, they all become pending.

rules.title: If the same trigger condition is met multiple times, the triggered effect becomes pending once for each time that con…
rules.text:
10.16.3. If the same trigger condition is met multiple times, the triggered effect becomes pending once for each time that condition is met.

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Unit’s effect text reads "When this Unit steals a Gig, increase it by up to 5.” In this example, the trigger is “When this Unit steals a Gig.” If the Unit steals 2 Gigs at the same time, then the effect “increase it by up to 5” becomes pending twice.

rules.title: Triggered effects may use timing labels such as [ATTACK], [CALL], [PLAY], or [DEFEATED], or timing text such as “when…
rules.text: 10.17. Triggered effects may use timing labels such as [ATTACK], [CALL], [PLAY], or [DEFEATED], or timing text such as “when,” “at the start of,” “at the end of,” and variations thereof. See TERMS > Trigger Keywords.

rules.title: If an effect instructs a player to choose, select, or otherwise make a choice, that choice is made when the effect in…
rules.text: 10.31. If an effect instructs a player to choose, select, or otherwise make a choice, that choice is made when the effect instructs the player to make that choice.

rules.title: If an effect requires a choice and no legal choice can be made, that choice is not made.
rules.text: 10.31.1. If an effect requires a choice and no legal choice can be made, that choice is not made.

rules.title: If an effect requires you to choose a specific number of targets, you must choose that number of targets.
rules.text: 10.31.2. If an effect requires you to choose a specific number of targets, you must choose that number of targets. If you can’t, choose as many valid targets as possible up to that number instead.

rules.title: If an effect requires a player to choose a number, that player must choose a non-negative whole number.
rules.text: 10.31.3. If an effect requires a player to choose a number, that player must choose a non-negative whole number.

rules.title: Draw
“Draw” is a game action in which you move the top card of your deck to your hand.
rules.text: 11.5.1. “Draw” is a game action in which you move the top card of your deck to your hand.

rules.title: When an effect says “Draw X” (where X is a number), take the draw action X number of times.
rules.text: 11.5.2. When an effect says “Draw X” (where X is a number), take the draw action X number of times. Literally, it means “move the top card of your deck to your hand, X individual times.”

rules.title: When you “Draw X,” draw each card individually.
rules.text: 11.5.2.1. When you “Draw X,” draw each card individually. Do not take multiple cards from the top of your deck at once.

rules.title: When you “Draw up to X,” choose the number of cards you will draw, then draw exactly that number of cards.
rules.text: 11.5.2.2. When you “Draw up to X,” choose the number of cards you will draw, then draw exactly that number of cards.

rules.title: If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, it counts as drawing from an empty deck.

decisions.first: First friendly Arasaka effective Unit declaration per controller/global turn, recorded even while Yorinobu is face-down/absent. The FAQ rules out first-since-reveal.
decisions.declaration: 9.3–9.5: target locked and attacker spent before ATTACK_DECLARED/history/discovery. Later Blocker/departure/invalidation does not undo declaration (9.6, 9.13, 9.26–9.29).
decisions.source: Face-up LEGENDS source only (3.4.1, 4.3). No numeric cost/power or Go Solo; no field entry.
decisions.classification: Exact immutable tag Arasaka (3.13.1); effective UNIT includes Goro in FIELD (4.2.1). Deck affiliation and Gear do not supply tags.
decisions.ordered: Draw, then test current Street Cred, then controller chosen discard. Existing effect continuation prevents interleaving (10.2.3,10.3.3).
decisions.null: 5.11.4.2 places Null below 0; therefore below the nonnegative threshold 20. Null is not converted to numeric zero.
decisions.reset: Each global turn, existing startTurn boundary; no cleanup/END-window reset.
decisions.discard: 10.31: controller discards from own hand; newly drawn card eligible; one option automatic; empty draw loss ends resolution.
decisions.saburo: Read-only next-candidate review. FAQ confirms attacking aura includes Fight/Steal; no Saburo admission.
